newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Shipping ban not appropriate - Australia Oppn.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Shipping ban not appropriate - Australia Oppn.

text.p: Australian Opposition Leader Kim Beazley said on Friday there were better ways for unions to protest against the arrest of two Indonesian labour leaders than to impose shipping bans.
"I can understand that members of the union movement would be concerned about what happens to unionists in other countries," Beazley told reporters.
"But I think the most effective means, and the most useful means of protest, is to get together the letters, to get together the direct approach to embassies, this type of activity."
The Maritime Union of Australia (MUA) imposed a ban on Indonesian cargo and shipping on Wednseday after the arrests of Indonesian labour leaders Muchtar Pakpahan and Dita Sari.

The union said the ban was also a response to Australian Prime Minister John Howard's failure to press Indonesia on human rights and democracy during his three-day visit there earlier this week. "On these types of issues, I think on the whole it would be better that people keep their protest activity within the forums of the normal political presentation," Beazley said.
